$comment: Copy this to <project>/.claude/gates.json and edit. It is the one place a
project says what its gates are; bin/gate runs them, guard.py refuses the
bare command that would print a gate's whole log into a session, and
statusline-extra.py reports which verdicts are green and how stale.
tier:   name, dir it runs in, cmd, and `watch` - the paths whose being
written since the verdict make that verdict stale.
guard:  regexes for the bare command this tier replaces. Optional.
env:    variables the gate needs and a person keeps forgetting.
refuses_port / requires_port: a gate that would damage something, or one
that would quietly run less than it claims. Both refuse; set a
force_env name to 1 to insist.
summary: how to get one line out of the log. `any` is tried whatever
happened, `pass` and `fail` only on theirs, and a `count` object
reports how many times a string appears.
checks: things a person runs by hand that still leave a verdict behind.
ports:  what the status line watches, as [port, label, glyph].
deny:   any other bare command this project would rather not see.
cheap_agents: agents the five-hour brake lets through even when the
window is nearly spent, because re-running one costs almost
nothing. Default: ["gate"].

requires_port.why: nothing is on :5432, so the database tests would not run.
